verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              सिन्धुराजे हते तात समरे सव्यसाचिना।  तथैव भूरिश्रवसि किमासीद्वो मनस्तदा॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said What, O Sanjaya, was the state of your mind when the king of Sindhu was slain in battle by Savyasachi and Bhurisrava (by Satyaki)?

verses.sanskrit: दुर्योधनेन च द्रोणस्तथोक्तः कुरुसंसदि। किमुक्तवान्परं तस्मै तन्ममाचक्ष्व सञ्जय॥२॥
verses.english: Relate to me, O Sanjaya, what Drona did say after he had been thus addressed by Duryodhana in the midst of the Kurus.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              निष्टानको महानासीत्सैन्यानां तव भारत। सैन्धवं निहतं दृष्ट्वा भूरिश्रवसमेव च॥३॥
मन्त्रितं तव पुत्रस्य ते सर्वमवमेनिरे। येन मन्त्रेण निहताः शतशः क्षत्रियर्षभाः॥४॥
verses.english: All of them censured the policy of your son, in virtue of which hundreds of foremost of men were destroyed.

verses.sanskrit: द्रोणस्तु तद्वचः श्रुत्वा पुत्रस्य तव दुर्मनाः। मुहूर्तमिव तद्ध्यात्वा भृशमार्तोऽभ्यभाषत॥५॥
verses.english: Drona too, hearing those words of your son, became sad at heart. Then, O king of kings, reflecting a moment he said very sorrowfully (these words).

verses.sanskrit:
द्रोण उवाच।
              दुर्योधन किमेवं मां वाक्शरैरपि कृन्तसि।  अजय्यं सततं संख्ये ब्रुवाणं सव्यचाचिनम्॥६॥
verses.english: Drona said O Duryodhana, why are you piercing me with words (keen) as darts? I have told you (repeatedly) that Savyasachi is uncognizable in battle.

verses.sanskrit: एतेनैवार्जुनं ज्ञातुमलं कौरव संयुगे। यच्छिखण्ड्यवधीद्भीष्मं पाल्यमानः किरीटिना॥७॥
verses.english: We have got (sufficient) proofs of what Arjuna is, when protected by Kiriti, Sikhandi slew Bhisma in battle, O Kaurava.

verses.sanskrit: अवध्यं निहतं दृष्ट्वा संयुगे देवदानवैः। तदैवाज्ञासिषमहं नेयमस्तीति भारती॥८॥
verses.english: Seeing that Bhishma, who could not be defeated by the celestials and the Danavas in battle, was slain (by Sikhandi), I understood that the Bharata army was doomed.

verses.sanskrit: यं पुंसां त्रिषु लोकेषु सर्वशूरममंस्महि। तस्मिन्निपतिते शूरे किं शेषं पर्युपास्महे॥९॥
verses.english: That person, whom we looked upon as the foremost of all the heroes in the three worlds, being slain, who else there that can inspire us with confidence?

verses.sanskrit: यां स्म तान् ग्लहते तात शकुनिः कुरुसंसदि। अक्षान्न तेऽक्षा निशिता बाणास्ते शत्रुतापनाः॥१०॥
verses.english: The dice with which Shakuni played in the assembly-hall of the Kurus, O affecnate one, are not (real) dice but their arrows destructive of foes, has ever been able to achieve.

verses.sanskrit: त एते घ्नन्ति नस्तात विशिखाः पार्थचोदिताः। तांस्तदाऽऽख्यायमानस्त्वं विदुरेण न बुद्धवान्॥११॥
यास्ता विजयतश्चापि विदुरस्य महात्मनः। धीरस्य वाचो नाश्रौषीः क्षेमाय वदतः शिवाः॥१२॥
verses.english: You did not then pay heed to those auspicious words, which the magnanimous wise Vidura with tearful eyes said for your good.

verses.sanskrit: तदिदं वर्तते घोरमागतं वैशसं महत्। तस्यावमानाद्वाक्यस्य दुर्योधन कृते तव॥१३॥
verses.english: In consequence of your disregard for those words, O Duryodhana, this dire, terrible and impending disaster has overtaken you.

verses.sanskrit: योऽवमन्य वचः पथ्यं सुहृदामाप्तकारिणाम्। स्वमतं कुरुते मूढः स शोच्यो न चिरादिव॥१४॥
verses.english: That stupid person, who disregarding the wholesome advice of his trusted friends, follows his own inclinations, is very soon reduced to a pitiable plight.

verses.sanskrit: यच्च नः प्रेक्षमाणानां कृष्णामानाय्य तत्सभाम्। अनर्हन्तीं कुले जातां सर्वधर्मानुचारिणीम्॥१५॥
तस्याधर्मस्य गान्धारे फलं प्राप्तमिदं महत्। नोचेत्पापं परे लोके त्वमर्च्छेथास्ततोऽधिकम्॥१६॥
verses.english: O son of Gandhari, this (calamity which you are now in) is the bitter fruit of that sinful act on your part. This (punishment) is but insignificant for in the world to come you will be visited with direr calamities.

verses.sanskrit: यच्च तान्पाण्डवान् द्यूते विषमेण विजित्य ह। प्राव्राजयस्तदारण्ये रौरवाजिनवाससः॥१७॥
verses.english: (This disaster is also the outcome of) your deceit by means of which you defeated the Pandavas at the game of dice and exiled them to the forest clad in deer-skin.
verses.bhavadeepa: नोचेदिति । परलोकेऽधिकः पापिनां क्लेश इह त्वल्पेनैव भोगेन निस्तार इति भावः ॥१६॥

verses.sanskrit: पुत्राणामिव चैतेषां धर्ममाचरतां सदा। द्रुह्येत्को नु नरो लोके मदन्यो ब्राह्मणब्रुवः॥१८॥
verses.english: Is there, in the world, any other Brahmana besides myself that would injure the (Pandavas) who devoted to righteousness and are (as dear) to me as my (own) sons.

verses.sanskrit: पाण्डवानामयं कोपस्त्वया शकुनिना सह। आहृतो धृतराष्ट्रस्य संमते कुरुसंसदि॥१९॥
दुःशासनेन संयुक्तः कर्णेन परिवर्धितः।  क्षत्तुर्वाक्यमनादृत्य त्वयाऽभ्यस्तः पुनः पुनः॥२०॥
verses.english: are ever Has been fostered by Dushasana together with Karna and had been repeatedly fanned by you who never paid regard to the words of Khattva.

verses.sanskrit: यत्ताः सर्वे पराभूताः पर्यवारयताऽर्जुनम्।  सिन्धुराजानमाश्रित्य स वो मध्ये कथं हतः॥२१॥
verses.english: How was it that you, who stood by the ruler by the Sindhu and tried your utmost to withstand Arjuna, were all defeated and why was he (Jayadratha) slain in your midst?

verses.sanskrit: कथं त्वयि च कर्णे च कृपे शल्ये च जीवति।  अश्वत्थाम्नि च कौरव्य निधनं सैन्धवोऽगमत्॥२२॥
युध्यन्तः सर्वराजानस्तेजस्तिग्ममुपासते। सिन्धुराजं परित्रातुं स वो मध्ये कथं हतः॥२३॥
verses.english: How was it that the king of Sindhu was slain in their midst, since for the purpose of rescuing him all the kings fought with fiery energy.

verses.sanskrit: मय्येव हि विशेषेण तथा दुर्योधन त्वयि।  आशंसत परित्राणमर्जुनात्स महीपतिः॥२४॥
verses.english: That lord of the earth looked especially to yourself and me for his rescue from Arjuna, O Duryodhana.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तस्मिन्परित्राणमलब्धवति फाल्गुनात्।  न किञ्चिद‌नुपश्यामि जीवितस्थानमात्मनः॥२५॥
verses.english: But he failed to have that rescue from (the clutches of) Arjuna. I too do not find any hope for my own life.

verses.sanskrit: मज्जन्तमिव चात्मान धृष्टद्युम्नस्य किल्बिषे।  पश्याम्यहत्वा पञ्चालान्सह तेन शिखण्डिना॥२६॥
verses.english: I see that I am (fast) sinking into the mire of Dhristadyumna's (cunning) until I can slay the Panchalas together with Sikhandi.

verses.sanskrit: तन्मां किमभितप्यन्तं वाक्शरैरेव कृन्तसि।  अशक्तः सिन्धुराजस्य भूत्वा त्राणाय भारत॥२७॥
verses.english: Since I myself am tormented with grief, wherefore are you piercing me with words (poignant) as an arrow, you who failed to rescue the king of Sindhu, O Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: सौवर्णं सत्यसन्धस्य ध्वजमक्लिष्टकर्मणः।  अपश्यन्युधि भीष्मस्य कथमाशंससे जयम्॥२८॥
मध्ये महारथानां च यत्राहन्यत सैन्धवः।  हतो भूरिश्रवाश्चैव किं शेषं तत्र मन्यसे॥२९॥
verses.english: Since the ruler of Sindhu and Bhurisrava have been slain from the very midst of the mighty-car-warriors, you can (very well) anticipate what the result will be.

verses.sanskrit: कृप एव च दुर्धर्षो यदि जीवति पार्थिव।  यो नागात्सिंन्धुराजस्य वर्त्म तं पूजयाम्यहम्॥३०॥
verses.english: O lord of the earth, if, without following the path of the king of Sindhu, the irresistible Kripa be still alive, I praise him highly (for his escape with life).

verses.sanskrit: यत्रापश्यं हतं भीष्मं पश्यतस्तेऽनुजस्य वै।  दुःशासनस्य कौरव्य कुर्वाणं कर्म दुष्करम्॥३१॥
verses.english: When, O Kaurava king, I behold that Bhishma, capable of achieving the most difficult exploits and unslayable even by the celestials together with Vasava in battle, was slain in your very sight and in that of your younger brother Dusasana, I thought, O king, that the earth no longer belonged to you.

verses.sanskrit: अवध्यकल्पं संग्रामे देवैरपि सवासवैः।  न ते वसुन्धराऽस्तीति तदाऽहं चिन्तये नृप॥३२॥
इमानि पाण्डवानां च सृञ्जयानां च भारत।  अनीकान्याद्रवन्ते मां सहितान्यद्य भारत॥३३॥
verses.english: Behold! O king, O Bharata, the troops of the Pandavas and those of the Srinjayas are jointly advancing against me.

verses.sanskrit: नाहत्वा सर्वपञ्चालान्कवचस्य विमोक्षणम्। कर्ताऽस्मि समरे कर्म धार्तराष्ट्र हितं तव॥३४॥
verses.english: I will not lay down my armour without destroying all the Panchalas; (and), O son of Dhritarashtra, I will perform which acts in battle as will benefit you.

verses.sanskrit: राजन् ब्रूयाः सुतं मे त्वमश्वत्थामानमाहवे।  न सोमकाः प्रमोक्तव्या जीवितं परिरक्षता॥३५॥
verses.english: O king! Go and convey my direction for Ashvatthama that he should battle taking all care of his life and not let go living Somakas at all possible efforts viz. he has to kill them all definitely.

verses.sanskrit: यच्च पित्राऽनुशिष्टोऽसि तद्वचः परिपालय।  आनृशंस्ये दमे सत्ये चाजवे च स्थिरो भव॥३६॥
धर्मार्थकामकुशलो धर्मार्थावप्यपीडयन्।  धर्मप्रधानकार्याणि कुर्याश्चेति पुनः पुनः॥३७॥
verses.english: Be diligent in (the exercise) religion, profit and pleasure without despising religion and profit and always perform those acts in which the exercise of religion is mostly required.

verses.sanskrit: चक्षुर्मनोभ्यां सन्तोष्या विप्राः पूज्याश्च शक्तितः। न चैषां विप्रियं कार्यं ते हि वह्निशिखोपमाः॥३८॥
एष त्वहमनीकानि प्रविशाम्यरिसूदन।  रणाय महते राजंस्त्वया वाक्शरपीडितः॥३९॥
verses.english: O destroyer of foes, afflicted as I am with your words darts I will now penetrate through the enemy's line in order to engage in a furious encounter (for your sake).

verses.sanskrit: त्वं च दुर्योधन बलं यदि शक्तोऽसि पालय।  रात्रावपि च योत्स्यन्ते संरब्धाः कुरुसृञ्जयाः॥४०॥
verses.english: As for your, O Duryodhana, if you are capable, go and protect your army, for both the Kurus and the Srinjayas, that are furious (with rage) will fight even during the night.

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा ततः प्रायाद्द्रोणः पाण्डवसृञ्जयान्।  मुष्णन् क्षत्रियतेजांसि नक्षत्राणामिवांशुमान्॥४१॥
verses.english: Having said thus, Drona, like the sun drawing out the energy of the stars, advanced against the Pandavas and the Srinjayas in order to destroy the energy of the Kshatriyas.
